newsitem.title: USA: Continental to hand out $68 million to employees.
newsitem.headline: Continental to hand out $68 million to employees.

text.p: While rival American Airlines slugs it out in negotiations with pilots to avoid a crippling strike, Continental Airlines said Thursday it would spend Valentine's Day handing out $68 million in profit-sharing checks to its 37,500 employees.
The checks were to be delivered on Friday by Continental Chairman Gordon Bethune in a ceremony at Houston Intercontinental Airport, the airline's main hub.
Bethune was to arrive at the event in an armored Brink's truck. A similar ceremony was to be held at Continental's hub in Newark, N.J.
Continental spokesman Dave Messing said the timing of the payout had nothing to do with Dallas-based American's problems and everything to do with keeping employees happy.
"It (the payout) was on the same date last year. We tie it in to Valentine's Day because it's kind of a fun day," he said.
Continental, which has emerged twice from bankruptcy but posted record profits in 1996, began the payouts last year to reward employees for helping the company achieve financial objectives.
Messing said last year's payout was about 3.5 percent of each employees salary, but this year it will be about 7 percent.

American Airlines was in tense negotiations in Washington on Thursday trying to reach a last-minute accord with its pilots, who are seeking a hefty pay raise. The pilots have threatened to go on strike Friday night if the two sides do not get an agreement.

Continental will find out soon enough if its attempts to engender good labor relations have the desired effect. Its pilots said last month that they, too, would be seeking a pay hike when contract negotiations begin in April.
